title: New humanoid robot Gene.01 has skin that can feel your touch
excerpt: Meet Gene.01, the robot with skin.
content_html:
A new humanoid robot debuted this week with a sensor-laden layer of "smart skin" designed to feel exactly where and how hard it's being touched...for industrial safety, of course.

The robot, called Gene.01, comes from Generative Bionics and debuted at AMD's Advancing AI conference in San Francisco. CNET senior video producer Jesse Orrall got hands-on time with the machine, and Orrall described the texture of the smart skin as similar to a neoprene wetsuit. (Disclosure: Mashable and CNET are both owned by the same parent company, Ziff Davis.)

Around its frame, the bot is outfitted with "full-body multimodal skin" that can sense "touch, proximity, force and temperature," according to Generative Bionics.

Mashable Light Speed

Per CNET's reporting, the skin senses touch using two kinds of sensors working together. The first are touch sensors capable of detecting contact, as well as the precise location and amount of pressure applied. Orrall wrote that squeezing the robot's arm triggered a live rendering on a nearby screen, lighting up at the exact spot being touched and darkening as more pressure was applied.

The second sensor type handles proximity rather than direct contact. These are known in the industry as time-of-flight (ToF) sensors, which work by emitting invisible light and measuring how long it takes to reflect back — effectively letting the robot sense something (or someone) before actual contact occurs. Orrall reported that waving a hand near the sensors produced a cluster of dots on the display screen that tracked with the hand movement, fading out as the hand moved away.

The practicality of the design, according to CNET, is collision avoidance. The hope is that these features will make it safer for industrial robots to work in close proximity to humans, whether on a factory floor or elsewhere. Generative Bionics reportedly views Gene.01 as an early platform, with plans to customize the amount and placement of smart skin, as well as the robot's hands, or "end effectors," depending on a client's specific use case.

As CNET noted, sensing the world is only half the equation — the harder problem still ahead is teaching the robot to act on that sensory data in real-time, something Generative Bionics says it's continuing to develop.

content_html_zh:
本周，一款新型人形机器人首次亮相，它配备了一层充满传感器的“智能皮肤”，旨在准确感知触摸的位置和力度……当然，是为了工业安全。

该机器人名为 Gene.01，来自 Generative Bionics，并在旧金山举行的 AMD Advancing AI 会议上首次亮相。 CNET 高级视频制作人杰西·奥拉尔 (Jesse Orrall) 亲身体验了这台机器，奥拉尔 (Orrall) 形容智能皮肤的质地类似于氯丁橡胶潜水衣。 （披露：Mashable 和 CNET 均属于同一母公司 Ziff Davis 所有。）

根据 Generative Bionics 的说法，该机器人的框架周围配备了“全身多模态皮肤”，可以感知“触摸、接近、力和温度”。

可混搭光速

根据 CNET 的报道，皮肤使用两种协同工作的传感器来感知触摸。 第一种是触摸传感器，能够检测接触以及施加的压力的精确位置和大小。 奥拉尔写道，挤压机器人的手臂会触发附近屏幕上的实时渲染，在被触摸的确切位置亮起，并随着施加更大的压力而变暗。

第二种传感器类型处理接近而不是直接接触。 这些在业内被称为飞行时间 (ToF) 传感器，其工作原理是发射不可见光并测量反射回来所需的时间，从而有效地让机器人在实际接触发生之前感知某物（或某人）。 奥拉尔报告说，在传感器附近挥动手会在显示屏上产生一簇点，这些点会随着手的移动而变化，随着手的移开而消失。

根据 CNET 的说法，该设计的实用性在于避免碰撞。 希望这些功能将使工业机器人能够更安全地与人类近距离工作，无论是在工厂车间还是其他地方。 据报道，Generative Bionics 将 Gene.01 视为一个早期平台，计划根据客户的具体用例定制智能皮肤的数量和位置，以及机器人的手或“末端执行器”。

正如 CNET 指出的，感知世界只是等式的一半——未来更困难的问题是教会机器人根据感知数据实时采取行动，Generative Bionics 表示它正在继续开发这一点。
